reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is demonstrating how to search for a restaurant, customize food, check out, and track a DoorDash delivery. The promo code is presented as an ordinary customer discount and referral promotion connected to that tutorial, rather than an investment, credential request, or other financial-participation offer. External coupon and social-media links are mentioned, but their destination behavior and further claims are not established.

If you need a discount code, please use mine above.

opening.argument: The video links a promised saving to a viewer action: the description tells first-time customers to use the creator's code, while the closing explicitly says to order through him to save money. That is not merely neutral app instruction; it directs a purchase through an externally promoted code. The description also says the creator had credit from referring many customers, reinforcing that participation benefits the promoter. This is a low-barrier reward offer tied to ordering and following the creator's promotional path.

citations.quote: If you're a first time customer, I'll have a coupon code at the end of this video
Since I referred many customers to DoorDash, I had some credit available to use.
If you need a discount code, please use mine above.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not answer the solicitation. The title itself includes a promo-code reference, and the description directs viewers to use the creator's code. The ordinary checkout demonstration supplies the action that makes the promised saving operative: a viewer is told to order through the promoter to receive it.

citations.quote: DoorDash Promo Coupon Code
If you need a discount code, please use mine above.
go ahead and order that through me and it'll save you some money on your first order.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows only a conventional first-order discount and referral promotion attached to a real food order. It does not show that viewers must pay the creator, provide credentials, or enter a deceptive claim process. The video demonstrates the order being submitted and delivered, while the stated benefit is simply saving money on that order.

citations.quote: This was a great way for me to order food for real cheap and make a video for new customers on how to use the app.
there's my order

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an unusually cheap purchase, referral-based account credit, multiple external coupon and social links, and a direct request to use the creator's code. The description says the food was ordered 'for real cheap,' explains that credits came from referring many customers, and provides several off-platform destinations. The video therefore uses the appearance of a successful everyday order to make an easy savings and referral pathway look trustworthy, even though the destinations and the terms of the benefit are not established.

citations.quote: This was a great way for me to order food for real cheap
Since I referred many customers to DoorDash, I had some credit available to use.
DoorDash Driver Promo Code - http://DashCashPromo.com Hungry? First Time Customer Order Promo - http://DashCoupon.com
Facebook Page: https://www.facebook.com/DashCashPromo/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the links as harmless before establishing what they do. The supplied description contains several external destinations, a first-time-customer promotion, and a referral-credit explanation, while the video emphasizes that the meal was effectively very cheap. Those signals are relevant to whether the ordinary-order presentation is being used to normalize a promotional acquisition funnel.

citations.quote: Hungry? First Time Customer Order Promo - http://DashCoupon.com
Online Shopping Coupons: http://bit.ly/DoorDashMike
food for real cheap

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals do not establish deception. The description openly identifies the links as promo, coupon, social-media, shopping-coupon, and product destinations, and it explains the claimed credit as arising from referrals. Cheap food and a referral discount are ordinary commerce facts, not evidence of a fabricated reward or an unsafe payment scheme.

opening.argument: The apparent instructional role functions as promotion because the tutorial repeatedly turns routine ordering into a reason to use the creator's code. The title combines an app walk-through with a promo-code label, the description asks viewers to use the code, and the closing directs first-time customers to order through the creator for savings. The practical demonstration is therefore a vehicle for steering viewers toward a linked discount and the promoter's referral pathway, rather than merely explaining the app.

citations.quote: How To Order Food Delivery with the DoorDash App Walk Thru - DoorDash Promo Coupon Code
If you need a discount code, please use mine above.
make sure you wait until the end, and go ahead and order that through me and it'll save you some money on your first order.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce label does not remove the promotional steering. The title expressly appends 'DoorDash Promo Coupon Code,' the description says the code helps the creator make new videos, and the closing asks viewers to wait until the end and order through him. Those are calls to participate, not incidental background to an independent demonstration.

citations.quote: DoorDash Promo Coupon Code
It helps me make new videos which I appreciate.
make sure you wait until the end

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and scam are not interchangeable. The content openly presents itself as a DoorDash ordering walk-through, and the cited request is for a normal first-order coupon. Nothing in these quotes shows that the app demonstration is false, that the discount is unavailable, or that viewers are asked for money or sensitive information outside the ordinary order.
